title: Months the published inspection files are nearly empty
question: Can the published inspection files show kitchen conditions during the emergency meal contracts?
finding: In 2019 the files hold about 972 inspections a month; April to June 2020 hold 70 in all, November 2019 holds 1, December 2019 to February 2020 and September to December 2023 hold none. The facilities at SMG's registered addresses (Moscone Center and Bill Graham Civic Auditorium) have 0 inspections dated April 2020 to June 2021 (76 in all years, none poor).
how: Distinct inspections per month across the three files (2016-2019 scores, 2020-2023, 2024 onward). Months under 150 are listed.
limits: Inspections were paused or reduced in the first months of the pandemic, and the change from the 2016-2019 scoring system to pass/fail explains the 2019-2020 break; the 2023 gap is the change to the 2024 file. Records may exist that the portal does not publish. The health department's schedule keeps food inspection reports 5 years (Citywide Records Retention Schedules, DataSF hy3m-hqsn).
